meta.title: Manoeuvre detection and characterisation
meta.authored_by: Claude Opus (illustrative draft, pending Ash authoring)
meta.change_reason: ILLUSTRATIVE content authored to exercise the drill loop, the scoring engine and the interface end to end. Derived only from public open-source material on space domain awareness practice, per the flight plan's public-sources rule. It is NOT a JCO procedure and has not been authored or validated by a subject-matter expert. Ash owns authoring and redaction sign-off; every step, threshold and answer key here is TBC, re-verify.

purpose: Establish whether an observed change in an object's orbit is a deliberate manoeuvre, characterise it, and decide whether it meets the threshold for reporting.
entry_conditions: An element set update places the object outside the predicted along-track position beyond sensor residual expectation.
A longitude drift rate change is observed on a geostationary object across consecutive fits.
An external cue reports a possible orbit change and correlation is requested.

steps.action: Confirm the change is present in more than one independent fit before treating it as real.
steps.note: A single fit can move on data quality alone. Two fits from different epochs is the cheapest discriminator available.

steps.action: Rule out a data artefact: check epoch spacing, near-duplicate epochs, and whether the residuals are consistent with the contributing sensors.
steps.warning: A very small epoch gap between fits produces an implied drift rate that is physically impossible. Treat an implausible rate as an artefact hypothesis of equal standing, not a footnote.

steps.action: Estimate the along-track and radial change and derive an approximate delta-v.
steps.note: Judge the figure against what the platform class could plausibly produce.

steps.action: Classify the manoeuvre as station-keeping, repositioning, or unattributed.
steps.note: Station-keeping is periodic and small. Repositioning changes the drift rate and holds the change.

steps.action: Check the object against the protected-object criteria held outside this application before deciding the reporting threshold.
steps.warning: This application never holds that list. Knowing the check exists and is mandatory is the trained behaviour; performing it requires the authoritative source.

steps.action: Raise the report at the threshold the criteria set, with the evidence and the stated confidence.
Task follow-up observations to confirm the new orbit and detect any second burn.

threshold_criteria.name: two-fit-confirmation
threshold_criteria.condition: The orbit change is present in at least two independent fits from different epochs.

threshold_criteria.name: artefact-excluded
threshold_criteria.condition: Epoch spacing and residuals are consistent with a real change rather than a fit artefact.

threshold_criteria.name: plausible-delta-v
threshold_criteria.condition: The implied delta-v is within the plausible capability of the platform class.

threshold_criteria.name: drift-rate-change-held
threshold_criteria.condition: A geostationary drift rate change persists across subsequent fits rather than reverting.

reporting_requirements: Object designator, epoch of the pre-manoeuvre and post-manoeuvre fits, and the contributing sensors.
Estimated delta-v with an uncertainty, never a bare number.
Classification with a stated confidence and the evidence it rests on.
Whether the protected-object check was performed, and by whom.

transition_rules.when: The manoeuvre closes range on another object and the closing geometry is controlled.
The apparent orbit change is accompanied by new associated objects.

closure_criteria: The new orbit is confirmed by follow-up observation and the object is back under routine custody.
The change is determined to be an artefact and the fit is corrected.
